prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1249; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision. The insured reports a front-end impact at a slow speed in a parking area, and the claimant was reported as a passenger in the other vehicle.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it and coverage was in force on the reported date of loss. No issues with the policy status were found.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision and matches the location and general sequence described by the insured.

Entry 4: Photos of both vehicles were reviewed. The damage is mostly consistent with the described impact, and the pattern of contact points lines up with a head-on collision at low speed.

Entry 5: Took a recorded statement from the other driver, who confirmed the accident happened as described. An independent witness also gave a matching account of the impact.

Entry 6: Claimant is now represented by counsel. All further contact will go through the attorney's office, and the representation letter is on file.

Entry 7: Received the claimant's medical records and the initial treatment notes. The reported back strain fits the kind and force of the crash well.

Entry 8: Records show the claimant was treated for the same body area within the last two years. That prior condition appears to add to the current complaints, and this is noted for the file.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. The treating provider's notes explain the reasons, and the timeline is being reviewed against standard recovery expectations.

Entry 10: Checked the vehicle's repair and inspection history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the coverage start date.

Entry 11: Each contact with the claimant, through the attorney and directly, has produced the same account of the accident. The file is being prepared for the next review with the medical and repair documentation attached.
